chapter_theme: A song at Vinayakamalai, Pillaiyarpatti (விநாயகமலை - பிள்ளையார்பட்டி): a litany of salutations to Murugan by his names, born in Saravana, son of Uma, root of this world and the next, asking only for grace, with praise of the vel that shook the worlds and of Vishnu and Brahma worshipping his feet.

584.reading: A song of salutations: the poet bows again and again (நமோநம) to Murugan as born in Saravana, lotus-footed, young and valiant, lord of the world, supreme form, king of the gods, wearer of fragrant kadamba, child of Uma, Kali and Bhagavati, root of this world and the next, and asks for grace. The praise shows the vel thrown so that dust rose to the sun, the seven seas cried out, Meru was shattered and the demons fell, and Vishnu, Brahma and Isa worshipping his feet, the lord on the peacock dwelling on Vinayakamalai, support of the forest people.
584.nuance: The plea is a litany in the form of a mantra of praise (நமோநம repeated twelve times), with no confession. இகபர மூலா: root of this world and the next. சமதளவூரா and வசுவெனும் ஆகார ஈசன் are not clear to me.

source_issues: Song 584: unflagged garble செர்ருபா (line 5), probably ஸ்வரூபா.
The heading joins two names, விநாயகமலை and பிள்ளையார்பட்டி; the song itself names only விநாயக மலை.
